subject.title: Clarify or preserve skill source provenance from CLI publish

question: Should CLI-provided GitHub source metadata remain non-visible, be retained only as explicitly unverified attribution, or gain a separately server-verified publish flow?
rationale: This choice determines the meaning of public provenance, the verification burden, and whether third parties may rely on a repository link as a trust signal; source inspection cannot safely choose that policy.

options.title: Add unverified attribution
options.body: Persist and display client-declared source separately from trusted provenance, with conspicuous unverified wording and no effect on verify or trust decisions.

options.title: Document non-visible metadata
options.body: Keep the current trust boundary and update CLI help, API docs, and publish output to say these fields do not create visible or trusted provenance.

options.title: Design verified CLI publishing
options.body: Add a server-side verification and file-match flow before CLI source data can become trusted provenance.

recommendation.title: Add unverified attribution
recommendation.body: Persist and display client-declared source separately from trusted provenance, with conspicuous unverified wording and no effect on verify or trust decisions.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged GitHub-backed source work is the closest existing ownership signal for the server-resolved provenance boundary.
